nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a fitting algorithm that maps a data vector $z$ of length $n + 1$ to a regression function $\hat\mu = A(z) : \mathcal X \to \mathbb{R}$. Its absolute residual score is $S(z)_i = \lvert y_i - \hat\mu(x_i) \rvert$, the residual of point $i$ under the fit trained on all $n + 1$ points. Evaluated on the augmented data $(z_1, \dots, z_n, (x, y))$, these are the residuals $R_{y,i}$ of Lei et al., equation (4),…
nodes.title: Absolute residual score of a fitting algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $z = (z_1, \dots, z_n)$ be $n$ data points $z_i = (x_i, y_i) \in \mathcal X \times \mathcal Y$, let $x$ be a test covariate, and let $S$ be a score map on augmented data vectors of length $n + 1$. For a trial response $y$, write $R^y = S(z_1, \dots, z_n, (x, y))$. The full conformal set at level $k$ is
nodes.title: Full conformal prediction set

nodes.summary: If the fitted regression function does not depend on the order of the data points, $A(z \circ \sigma) = A(z)$ for every permutation $\sigma$, then the absolute residual score is permutation equivariant. The full conformal coverage theorems therefore apply to the regression set of Lei et al., equations (4) and (7), up to the treatment of ties discussed on the page of the full conformal prediction set.
nodes.title: Residuals of a symmetric algorithm are equivariant

nodes.summary: A map $S$ from data vectors $z = (z_1, \dots, z_{n+1})$ to score vectors in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is permutation equivariant if permuting the data points permutes the scores in the same way: $S(z \circ \sigma) = S(z) \circ \sigma$ for every permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1, \dots, n+1\}$.
nodes.title: Permutation-equivariant score map

nodes.summary: Let the law $\mu$ of the data vector $(Z_1, \dots, Z_{n+1})$ be invariant under every coordinate permutation, and let the score map $S$ be measurable and permutation equivariant. Then the law of the score vector $S(Z)$ is invariant under every coordinate permutation. Indeed, $S(Z) \circ \sigma = S(Z \circ \sigma)$, and $Z \circ \sigma$ has the same law as $Z$.
nodes.title: Equivariant scores of exchangeable data are exchangeable

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of full conformal coverage, if moreover the $n + 1$ scores $S(Z)$ are almost surely distinct, then for $0 \le \alpha < 1$ the full conformal set at level $k = \lceil (1 - \alpha)(n + 1) \rceil$ covers $Y_{n+1}$ with probability at most $1 - \alpha + 1/(n + 1)$. Together with the lower bound, full conformal prediction is valid and nearly exact: its coverage lies in…
nodes.title: Upper bound on full conformal coverage without ties

nodes.summary: Let the law $\mu$ of the data vector $(Z_1, \dots, Z_{n+1})$, with $Z_i = (X_i, Y_i)$, be a probability measure invariant under every coordinate permutation; an i.i.d. law is an example. Let the score map $S$ be measurable and permutation equivariant. Then for $0 \le \alpha < 1$ the full conformal set built from the first $n$ points at level $k = \lceil (1 - \alpha)(n + 1) \rceil$ covers $Y_{n+1}$ at $X_{n+1}$ with…
nodes.title: Full conformal coverage

nodes.summary: For a data vector $Z = (Z_1, \dots, Z_{n+1})$ with $Z_{n+1} = (X_{n+1}, Y_{n+1})$, the event $Y_{n+1} \in C_k(Z_1, \dots, Z_n; X_{n+1})$ equals the event that the last coordinate of the score vector $S(Z)$ is at most the $k$-th smallest of its first $n$ coordinates. The reason is that at the true response $y = Y_{n+1}$ the augmented data set $(Z_1, \dots, Z_n, (X_{n+1}, y))$ is $Z$ itself.
nodes.title: Full conformal coverage event as a split conformal event
